text: The case list of the write-off stage, the ACE batch status of source ALS, the balance, the WO rule package and the case-move answer are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and only rwb-case writes recovery_case, while rwb-decision governs the rule rows; R-WO-01 names v_ace_batch_status, which this service may not read. TSD S7 T5.2 names the interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name for these rows, so no name may be invented. The plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.

text: The two tracks of R-WO-01 are the pursue track and the sale track that the route set's end states name; the criterion that separates them is published by no source, so the scan applies the one eligibility rule and the tax criteria to every open case and records the package version, and it invents no per-track test.
why: Legacy AC2 and R-WO-01 say 'on both tracks' and no source defines them. The route set's end states name 'the pursue track' and 'sold to a buyer as a charged-off population', and R-WO-29 and R-WO-32 are the rows that choose a track after posting, so a per-track eligibility test would be a business rule invented here.

text: The monthly clock of the scan is a Temporal Schedule on queue rwb-writeoff that replaces JOB-16 and fires on the third working day, with its identifier, its hour and the definition of the third working day unstated; DP-10 is absent from the pattern set, so the Schedule is built, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is recorded as an absent H row and the contract story declares the trigger without registering it.
why: The ownership rows give S7 one job, JOB-16 write-off scan, and the Batch and Scheduling Design gives it as monthly on the third working day with two hold conditions; DP-10 is the pattern that converts Quartz into a Temporal Schedule and the plan does not carry it or its kit row. Registering nothing in the contract story keeps the CON free of build work.
